subject: Urban Planning
subcategory: Parks, Green Spaces, and Public Land
title: Blue-Green Networks
description: A short lesson to help you apply Blue-Green Networks.

hook.text: Copenhagen plans to be carbon neutral by 2025. Its strategy links green parks and blue waterways into one system.

buildup.text: Blue-green networks integrate rivers, canals, wetlands, and parks into a single ecological and recreational system.

discovery.text: They manage flooding, cool cities, support biodiversity, and provide recreation — all from the same infrastructure.

twist.text: Traditional engineering treats water as a problem to pipe away. Blue-green design treats water as a resource to keep.

climax.text: Singapore's ABC Waters program turned concrete drains into 100 naturalized waterways with parks alongside.

punchline.text: Connect the park and the river. Watch the whole city benefit.

quiz.question: What makes blue-green networks different from traditional water management?
options: They use colored pipes to distinguish water types underground
They treat water as a resource to keep, not a problem to pipe away
They separate stormwater from sewage using parallel pipe systems
